en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.18. Uppannattika (The Triplet on the Arisen)
Section on Analysis:
Root.
A arisen state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an arisen state: arisen roots are [root-conditions] for their associated states.

The roots are a condition by way of root-condition for the aggregates and for the mind-originated material phenomena. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the roots that have arisen are a condition by way of root-condition for the associated aggregates and for the kamma-produced material phenomena.
Object...
A arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
One contemplates the arisen eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes it and delights in it. Taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises...
[and so on] ...restlessness arises... [and so on] ...grief arises. [The same applies to] the arisen ear...

One contemplates the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … flavors … tangibles … the physical base … and the arisen aggregates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self … [and so on] … mental grief arises.
With the divine eye one sees a visible form; with the divine ear-element one hears a sound. The visible-form base [is the condition] for eye-consciousness … [and so on] …
The sphere of the tangible is related to body-consciousness ... [and so on] ... arisen aggregates are related to knowledge of supernormal power and to advertence by way of object-condition.
A non-arisen state is related to an arisen state by way of object-condition: non-arisen forms ... [and so on].
In sounds … in odors … in tastes … in tangibles … one contemplates unarisen aggregates as impermanent,
suffering, and non-self … [and so on] … grief arises. Unarisen aggregates are related to knowledge of the supernormal powers, knowledge of the minds of others,
knowledge of future states, and advertence by way of object condition.
A state that is arising (uppādī) is a condition, by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya), for a state that has arisen (uppanna):
the eye that is arising … [and so on] … the body; visible forms … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical basis (vatthu);

[or] regarding the aggregates that are arising as impermanent, suffering, and non-self … [and so on] … sorrow arises. The aggregates that are arising are conditions for the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power (iddhividhañāṇa) and for the knowledge of penetration of minds (cetopariyañāṇa).
Knowledge of the future is related to advertence by way of object-condition.
Dominance:
An arisen state is related to an arisen state by way of dominance-condition—namely, object-dominance and conascence-dominance.
Object-predominance: Having treated as important the eye that has arisen, one relishes it and delights in it;

taking that as important, lust arises, and wrong view arises. Having treated as important the ear that has arisen … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical basis … the aggregates that have arisen, one relishes them and delights in them.
One rejoices; taking that as an object, lust arises... [etc. ...Conascent predominance:
a predominant state that has arisen is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A non-arisen state is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for an arisen state. Object-predominance: in regard to what has not yet arisen...
Regarding forms … sounds … smells … tastes … tangibles … one esteems, relishes, and delights in unarisen aggregates;
by esteeming them, lust arises and wrong view arises.

A state that has arisen is a condition for a state that has arisen by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*): [the same applies to] what has arisen.
Taking the eye … the body … forms … tangibles … the physical basis … and the aggregates that have arisen as an object of esteem, one relishes them and delights in them;
taking them as an object of esteem, lust arises and wrong view arises.
Co-nascence.
An arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of co-nascence condition:

one arisen aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition …pe… two aggregates are conditions for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate that has arisen is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for three aggregates and for the matter produced by kamma (*kaṭattā-rūpa*) ...
[and so on] ... two aggregates are conditions, by way of co-nascence condition, for two aggregates and for the matter produced by kamma.
The aggregates are a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for the physical basis (*vatthu*); the physical basis is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for the aggregates.

Condition: One great primary element is a condition for three great primary elements by way of co-nascence condition … two great primary elements … [and so on] … Great primary elements are a condition for mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter by way of co-nascence condition.
External … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … one great primary element of non-percipient beings … [is a condition].
…pe… two great elements …pe… the great elements are a condition for kamma-produced matter and derived matter by way of co-nascence condition.
Mutuality:
An arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of mutuality condition—a single arisen aggregate [is a condition for the other three].

Three aggregates are related to one another by way of mutuality condition … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate that has arisen is related to three aggregates and the physical basis by way of mutuality condition.
Two aggregates … aggregates are related to the physical basis by way of mutuality condition. The physical basis is related to the aggregates … [by way of mutuality condition].

Conditioned by way of mutuality condition: one great primary element … [and so on] … external … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … one great primary element of non-percipient beings is a condition for three great primary elements by way of mutuality condition … two great primary elements … [and so on].
A state that has arisen is a condition, by way of dependence-condition, for a state that has arisen: one arisen aggregate is a condition, by way of dependence-condition,
for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter …pe… two [aggregates are conditions for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter].
The aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … the aggregates [are related] to the physical basis,

the physical basis [is related] to the aggregates … one great primary … external … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … one great primary of non-percipient beings … the great primaries [are related] to mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter.

The eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness ... [and so on] ... the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness ... [and so on] ... the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition, by way of support-condition (nissayapaccaya), for the aggregates that have arisen.
Strong-dependence (upanissaya).
A arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*):
as object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [as appropriate] … Natural decisive support:

depending on an arisen temperature (*utu*), one produces jhāna, insight (*vipassanā*) … the path (*magga*) … direct knowledge (*abhiññā*) … attainment (*samāpatti*); one conceives conceit (*māna*) and adopts wrong view (*diṭṭhi*).

Depending on a meal that has arisen … [and so on] … depending on a lodging, one arouses jhāna, arouses insight … [and so on] … the path … [and so on] … direct knowledge … [and so on] … attainment; one conceives conceit, adopts wrong view.
Depending on temperature that has arisen … a meal … a lodging … on faith that has arisen … [and so on] … on wisdom, on bodily pleasure, on bodily …
It is a condition for suffering, the path, and the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A non-arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) …pe… Natural decisive support:
one aspiring for the perfection of beauty in a future life gives a gift.

One gives a gift, undertakes moral discipline, and performs the Uposatha rite. Aspiring for the attainment of sound not yet arisen... the attainment of fragrance not yet arisen... the attainment of flavor not yet arisen...

the attainment of tangible objects not yet arisen, and aspiring for aggregates not yet arisen, one gives a gift, undertakes moral discipline, and performs the Uposatha rite. [Likewise] the attainment of beauty not yet arisen... and so on... the aggregates not yet arisen.
Faith that has arisen … pe … wisdom, bodily pleasure, bodily pain, the Path,

and the attainment of the Fruit are related to [their respective subsequent states] by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). A state that is arising is related to a state that has arisen by way of decisive support condition— namely, as object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Natural strong-dependence … [and so on] … Natural strong-dependence: aspiring for the attainment of the eye that has arisen, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, and performs the observance-day duty.
Aspiring for the attainment of the ear … [and so on] … the body … beauty … fragrance … flavor … tangibles … the aggregates that have arisen.
One who aspires gives a gift, undertakes moral discipline, and performs the observance-day rites (*uposathakamma*).

There arises the attainment of the eye … [and so on] … the attainment of the body … the attainment of beauty … [and so on] … the attainment of tangibles … there arise the aggregates for one who has arisen faith … [and so on] … wisdom, bodily pleasure, bodily pain, the Path, and the attainment of the Fruit.
Condition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A pre-arisen phenomenon that has arisen is a condition for a phenomenon that has arisen by way of pre-arisen condition (*purejāta-paccaya*)— namely, as an object-pre-arisen condition (*ārammaṇa-purejāta*).
Base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: the eye … [as before] … one contemplates the base as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
one relishes it and delights in it; with that as object, lust arises … [as before] … grief arises.
By means of the divine eye, one sees a form; by means of the divine ear-element, one hears a sound. The visible-form base [is related] to eye-consciousness … [as before].
... pe ... the sense base of tangibles is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-arising condition (*purejātapaccaya*).

As for the pre-arising condition of the physical basis (*vatthupurejāta*): the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness ... pe ... the physical basis is a condition for arisen aggregates by way of pre-arising condition. Subsequently-arisen [condition] (*pacchājāta*)...
An arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of postnascence condition: arisen postnascent aggregates are a condition for this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.
Kamma:
An arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of kamma condition: arisen volition is a condition for its associated states...

Volition is a condition for the aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, volition that has arisen is a condition for its associated aggregates and for the kamma-born matter by way of kamma-condition.
Resultant...
An arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of resultant condition (*vipāka-paccaya*):
one arisen resultant aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition; ... two aggregates ...;
at the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*), one arisen aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for [kamma-]produced matter ...
Of forms … [and so on] … two aggregates … [and so on] … the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis by way of the resultant condition (*vipākapaccaya*).
Nutriment Condition: An arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of the nutriment condition (*āhārapaccaya*)—the arisen nutriments [are conditions] for their associated states.
The aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of nutriment-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking ...
[etc. ... Edible food is a condition for this body by way of nutriment-condition. Faculty [condition]...
An arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of the faculty-condition (*indriya-paccaya*).
Arisen faculties are a condition by way of the faculty-condition for their associated aggregates (*khandha*) and for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*).

At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*) … [and so on] … the eye-faculty is a condition for eye-consciousness … the body-faculty is a condition for body-consciousness … the material life-faculty … [and so on].
Material phenomena produced by kamma (kaṭattārūpa) are related to [other] material phenomena by way of the faculty condition (indriya-paccaya).
A arisen state is related to an arisen state by way of the jhāna condition … by way of the path condition (magga-paccaya).
… a condition by way of association-condition … a condition by way of dissociation-condition—conascent, prenascent, and postnascent.
Conascent: arisen aggregates are a condition by way of dissociation-condition for mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, arisen aggregates are a condition by way of dissociation-condition for kamma-produced matter.
The aggregates are related to the physical basis, and the physical basis is related to the aggregates, by way of dissociation condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*).
As pre-arisen: the eye-base to eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the body-base to body-consciousness; the physical basis is related to arisen aggregates by way of dissociation condition.
As post-arisen: arisen aggregates are related to this pre-arisen body by way of dissociation condition.
An arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of presence condition:
conascent, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. Conascent: one arisen aggregate is [a condition] for three aggregates...
And it is a condition, by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*), for mind-originated material phenomena ... [etc. ... two aggregates ... [etc. ... at the moment of rebirth-linking ...
[etc. ... one great primary element ... [etc. ... external ... nutriment-originated ... temperature-originated ... of non-percipient beings ... [etc. ... Pre-arisen:
through the contemplation of the eye as impermanent ... [etc. ... through the contemplation of the physical basis (*vatthu*) as impermanent ... sorrow arises.
One sees a form with the divine eye; one hears a sound with the divine ear-element.
The visible-form base is a condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*).

The eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness … [and so on] … the physical basis (*vatthu*) is a condition for arisen aggregates by way of presence-condition.
Condition: Postnascent arisen aggregates are a presence condition for this prenascent body.
Edible food is a presence condition for this body. The material life-faculty is a presence condition for kamma-produced matter.
A state that has not disappeared is a condition, by way of non-disappearance condition, for a state that has arisen … [etc.
… Chapter on Enumeration.
In the pure root condition, there is one; in the object condition, three; in the predominance condition, three; in the conascence condition, one; in the mutuality condition, one;

in the dependence condition, one; in the strong-dependence condition, three; in the prenascence condition, one; and in the postnascence, kamma, resultant, nutriment, faculty, and jhāna conditions [there is one].
In the path, with the associated, the dissociated, the presence, and the non-disappearance [conditions], there is one. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive.
Negative Extraction.
An arisen state is a condition for an arisen state by way of object-condition, conascence-condition,
decisive-support-condition, prenascence-condition, postnascence-condition,
nutriment-condition, and faculty-condition.
A state that has not yet arisen is a condition for a state that has already arisen by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya) and by way of decisive support-condition (upanissayapaccaya).
A state subject to arising is a condition for a state that has already arisen by way of object-condition … and by way of decisive support-condition.
1.18.7.2. Negative Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya)
In the Enumeration Chapter, under the Pure [Dependent Relation]:

three for not-root, three for not-object, three for not-predominance … pe … three for not-dissociation, two for not-presence, three for not-absence, three for not-disappearance, and two for not-non-disappearance. (Thus it should be counted.)
Negative (Paccanīya). 1.18.7.3.
Positive-Negative (Paccayānulomapaccanīya).
With root condition (hetupaccaya), there is one [condition] for the non-object (na-ārammaṇa) ... pe ... one for the non-absence (non-atthi) and the non-disappearance (no-vigata).
Positive-Negative.
1.18.7.4. Negative-Positive.

With not-root condition, there are three [results] in relation to object, three in relation to predominance, one in relation to conascence, one in relation to mutuality, and one in relation to dependence.
One [condition], three in the case of decisive support (upanissaya), one in the case of prenascence (purejāta), one in the case of postnascence (pacchājāta), and one each in the cases of kamma,
result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance.
This concludes the negative-positive (paccanīyānuloma) method.
The Triplet on Arisen is finished.
